newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FORECAST-Meralco '96 net seen up 18.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Meralco '96 net seen up 18.5 pct.

text.p: Manila Electric Co (Meralco), the Philippines' biggest power distributor, is expected to post a net profit of 5.2258 billion pesos in 1996, up 18.47 percent from 1995's 4.411 billion pesos, according to a Reuters poll.

Five Manila brokerage houses surveyed this week also said that Meralco will continue to register increased profits in 1997 at 6.336 billion pesos on the back of higher sales and income from non-core business.

"The more than 11 percent sales growth for the first 11 months of 1996 compared to the same period in 1995 was way above the expectations of most analysts. When the year started, we were only looking at a 10.4 percent growth," said Cecilio Castro, assistant manager at Anscor Hagedorn Securities Inc.
Meralco's sales rose by 11.6 percent in the first 11 months of 1996. Analysts put full-year growth at about 12 percent.

"Meralco's profits for every quarter of 1996 were in line with growth projections. Meralco's sales have always been linked to GDP and with the uptick on economic activity this year and in 1997, we expect Meralco to benefit further," said Alexis Cabel, an analyst at AngPing & Associates Securities Inc.
As a rule of thumb, a one percentage point increase in Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth translates to a 1.5 to 1.6 times increase in sales volume for Meralco, the analysts said.
The Philippines has predicted about 6.5 percent GDP growth in 1996, up from 5.7 percent in 1995.

"For 1997, profits will come primarily from higher sales. The nice thing about Meralco is that its earnings are secure. There's a captive market," said Raul Ruiz, assistant vice-president at Sun Hung Kai Securities.
Meralco serves close to three million customers in its franchise area, which includes the densely populated Metropolitan Manila.
But Meralco senior vice-president Benito de la Cruz told Reuters that in 1997, the company expects electricity sales to grow only by eight to 10 percent.

"We will be comparing 1997 with a higher sales base in 1996 so we should not expect spectacular sales growth this year. In 1995, we had two typhoons towards the end of the year and in 1996 we had none of those, hence the higher sales growth," de la Cruz added.
Saturnino Mejia, research head at Guoco Securities, said that the non-power business of Meralco will start to contribute to the company's revenues next year.

Although the development of a Meralco property in Makati City, Manila's financial district, into a mixed-use commercial and residential centre will be completed only towards the end of the century, pre-selling on towers and condominium units was conducted last year and will be booked in 1997, analysts said.
Meralco's de la Cruz said that the property venture of the company will contribute 10 to 20 percent of total revenues for 1997.
"Profits for 1996 will be fairly close to the 17 to 18 percent increase projected by most brokers," De la Cruz added.
The following were the brokerage houses surveyed and their corresponding net income and total revenues projections:

(in billion pesos)
